title: Impact of sterilization methods on dissolved trace metals concentrations in complex natural samples: Optimization of UV irradiation
author: Chifflet, Quéméneur, et al.

steps.title: Wear protective gloves and clean lab
steps.instruction: Wear powder‑free nitrile gloves at all times and keep the working area as clean as possible to avoid trace‑metal contamination.

steps.title: Condition new HDPE jerrycans
steps.instruction: Fill each HDPE jerrycan with Decon detergent and let stand for at least 48 h; then rinse five times with deionized water (DIW) or reverse‑osmosis water (ROW).

steps.title: Acid‑wash HDPE jerrycans
steps.instruction: Fill the jerrycans with 1 % v/v analytical‑grade HCl and let stand for at least 48 h; rinse five times with ultra‑pure MilliQ water; store the jerrycans filled with MilliQ in a cleaned plastic box or bag until use.

steps.title: Pre‑condition new bottles (BG, PET, FEP)
steps.instruction: Soak new bottles for at least 48 h in Decon, then rinse thoroughly seven times with DIW or ROW before the main cleaning procedure.

steps.title: Acid‑wash bottles
steps.instruction: Submerge BG, PET, or FEP bottles in a 10 % v/v analytical‑grade HCl bath; sonicate for 2 h **or** leave in the bath for at least 48 h; rinse five times with ultra‑pure MilliQ water; fill bottles with 0.1 % v/v ultrapure‑grade HCl, seal in zip‑locked plastic bags, and store in a trace‑metal clean‑room or under a laminar‑flow cabinet.

steps.title: Prepare coastal marine microcosms
steps.instruction: In triplicate (n = 3) place either no sediment (0 g L⁻¹) or sediment to achieve 10 g L⁻¹ in BG or FEP bottles, add the appropriate volume of coastal marine water sample, and seal the bottles.

steps.title: Apply UV irradiation
steps.instruction: Expose the bottles to UV light for 4 h (single exposure) or perform four cycles of 4 h UV followed by 24 h dark (4 h UV/24 h × 4). Include a biotic control with 0 h UV exposure. During UV exposure, manually shake each bottle every 30 min.

steps.title: Filter samples after UV
steps.instruction: After the UV treatment, filter each sample through a 0.2 µm syringe filter inside an ISO‑5 cleanroom.

steps.title: Analyze dissolved trace metals
steps.instruction: Inject the filtered extracts directly into an Argon‑Gas‑Dilution ICP‑MS (Thermo Scientific iCAP‑Q) operating in direct‑injection mode. Quantify Al, As, Cd, Co, Cr, Cu, Fe, Mo, Ni, Pb, Rb, Sb, Se, U, V, and Zn. Note that Cr and Se may be below the limit of detection and therefore not reported.

steps.title: Assess cell viability (optional)
steps.instruction: Count viable, damaged, and compromised cells by epifluorescence microscopy and flow cytometry (BD Bioscience FACSCalibur) using the NADS protocol; refer to Table S4 for detailed counting parameters.

description: The influence of UV irradiation was also considered in batch experiments conducted in triplicate (n = 3) on coastal marine samples without or with sediments (sediments/water 0 or 10 g/L, respectively), in two types of bottles (BG or FEP). According to the results obtained on lacustrine samples, a 4 h-UV irradiation was chosen to achieve a complete sterilization and compared to a biotic control (UV exposure: 0 h). During tests, BG and FEP bottles were shaken manually every 30 min. The samples stability was also monitored after 4 cycles of UV exposure (4 h UV/24 h). The quantification of viable, damaged or compromised cells within the free-bacterial community was also assessed by epifluorescence microscopy with flow cytometry counting (BD Bioscience® FACSCalibur) using the NADS protocol [[22], [23], [24]]. The details of cells counting are presented as additional information (Table S4). Very reproducible results were obtained whatever the bottle type and sediments/water condition used (Fig. 6a). However, concerning the effectiveness of UV sterilization, differences were observed between BG and FEP bottles. Indeed, a 4-hours UV exposure was efficient to eliminate the most of the microorganisms in FEP bottles (98% and 95% of cells mortality for 0 and 10 g/L sediments/water conditions, respectively), but was not effective in BG bottles (20% and 34% of cells mortality for 0 and 10 g/L sediments/water conditions, respectively). However, the large majority of live cells was eliminated (>98% loss) in both BG and FEP bottles from both 0 and 10 g/L sediments/water conditions by repeating this batch experiments with 4 cycles of UV exposure (4 h UV/24 h) (Fig. 6b).Fig. 6Variations of microorganisms viability (alive cells) in coastal marine samples (Bay of Marseille), in both sediments/water (0 and 10 g/L) and exposed to two UV irradiation time: 0 or 4 h (a), and 0 or after 4 cycles repeating 4 h at interval of 24 h.
